clue.text: Crime spree essentially gatecrashing fleet?

indicators.note: a gatecrasher pushes in uninvited, so the core letters are forced inside the word for fleet

parts.note: fleet means fast, pacy

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its heart, so only the central letter of each of crime and spree is taken

explanation.surface: A wave of crime breaks out when uninvited raiders burst in on a fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: I and R, the central letters of 'Crime' and 'spree', go inside PACY, and the whole clue describes the answer, a crime spree preying on ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Piracy is robbery at sea, the classic crime committed against a fleet of merchant ships.

clue.text: Relish cream on latte, just coating

parts.note: the cream of anything is its pick, the best

indicators.note: only the coat, the outside letters, of latte

explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A pickle is a relish, a tangy preserved condiment served alongside food.

clue.text: Rat on undeveloped boozer perhaps creating dirt

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to inform on an underage drinker you would report their age
second meaning: journalism dishing out the dirt, news reporting

explanation.surface: Informing on a pub still under construction stirs up dirt.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as REPORT AGE, the answer cryptically describes snitching on a drinker who is under age.
explanation.definitionFit: Reportage is news reporting, which in tabloid form means digging up dirt on people.

clue.text: Fellow on good terms with model makes a fortune

parts.note: CO- is a prefix for a fellow or partner, as in co-worker
to be in with someone is to be on good terms
a model sits for an artist

explanation.surface: A man who gets on well with a fashion model becomes rich.
explanation.definitionFit: To coin it is an informal idiom for earning lots of money quickly.

clue.text: Language Argentine associated with business staff

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
to staff is to man
Che Guevara, the revolutionary, was Argentine

explanation.surface: A South American tongue is linked with a firm's workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Argentine' comes first in the clue but its piece goes last; 'associated with' just joins it on.
explanation.definitionFit: Comanche is the tongue of the Comanche people of the southern Great Plains, a Uto-Aztecan language.

clue.text: Old farm hands, in exotic lands, lifted

indicators.note: in a down clue lifted means raised, read upwards
the answer lands within these words, held inside them

explanation.surface: Old farm workers in faraway countries are lifted up.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading upwards through 'in exotic' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxen were used to pull ploughs, so they were the workers of old-time farming.

clue.text: Boss's Yorkshire town house, always hard to ignore

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so the letter goes

parts.note: Hawes is a market town in the Yorkshire Dales
a house is a home
H for hard in each case, from both words

explanation.surface: The boss's house in a Yorkshire town is always hard to miss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' is slang for excellent. Hawes is a small market town in Wensleydale; dropping H from it and from HOME leaves AWES and OME.
explanation.definitionFit: Boss is slang, especially in Liverpool, for great or excellent, which awesome also means.

clue.text: Examined how some wine is sold

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... a place, inspected it before a robbery
second meaning: packed in cases of twelve bottles

explanation.walkthrough: Casing a joint is slang for checking it out before a burglary.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both criminal slang for scouting out a target and a description of bottles boxed in cases.

clue.text: Soon hosts set to broadcast shipping forecast feature?

indicators.note: to host is to hold within

parts.note: soon means early

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Presenters are ready to go on air shortly with the shipping forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: The shipping forecast is a BBC radio bulletin of sea conditions around Britain, giving wind directions.
explanation.definitionFit: An easterly is a wind from the east, a direction routinely given in the shipping forecast.

clue.text: Knockout involving leader of Premiership?

indicators.note: to involve here is to take in, so the first letter goes inside the word for a knockout

parts.note: a knockout is a stunning woman, a cutie

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cup match featuring a top-flight football club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knockout' is used twice over: as a stunner it gives CUTIE, around P; read with the whole clue it is a knockout football match that might include a Premiership side.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup tie is a match in a knockout competition such as the FA Cup, where the loser goes out.

clue.text: What's written by poet in residence over one misfortune

definitions.note: more than one misfortune, so a plural noun

indicators.note: the poet's output sits within the abbreviation for residence

parts.note: a poet writes verse

explanation.surface: A poet in residence writes about a stroke of bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over one' is part of the definition: more than one misfortune means a plural, setbacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverses are setbacks or changes for the worse, so several reverses are several misfortunes.

clue.text: Sweet dance one studied

parts.note: the rumba is a Cuban dance
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is one who has studied

explanation.surface: A dancer who is also a student is lovely.
explanation.definitionFit: A rum baba is a dessert, a small yeast cake soaked in rum syrup.

clue.text: Spiky thing, playing London team, chopped

parts.note: to lark is to play about, frolic

indicators.note: chopped means cut short, so the team's last letter goes

parts.note: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club

explanation.surface: A spiky character, fooling around, plays a London side and gets cut down.
explanation.walkthrough: SPURS is Tottenham Hotspur, a north London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkspur, the delphinium, carries its flowers on tall spikes, and each flower has a spur.

clue.text: Enthusiast over lunch who's hostile about cricket match

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the enemy goes around the match

parts.note: one who is hostile is a foe
ODI is a One Day International, a cricket match

explanation.surface: A lunchtime enthusiast turns hostile over a cricket fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: An ODI is a one-day international, a limited-overs cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: A foodie is a gourmet who takes keen pleasure in eating, so a lunch would excite one.

clue.text: Rubbish pastry, papa's common complaint

indicators.note: the letter is held in common, shared between the two words, so only one copy is kept

parts.note: scrap is rubbish, waste
a pie is a pastry
Papa is P in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: Bad pastry is Dad's usual grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: SCRAP and PIE overlap, sharing their P; 'common' says the Papa is shared, not doubled.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrapie is a disease, a complaint in the medical sense, affecting sheep and goats.

clue.text: Sort of cleaner relative endorsed on phone defaced TV part

indicators.note: heard over the phone, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: an aunt or auntie is a relative; to endorse something is to back it, so backed

indicators.note: defaced means losing its face, the front letter

parts.note: an aerial is the part of a TV set-up that picks up the signal

explanation.surface: A relative endorses a product on the phone while a part of the TV is damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auntie backed' spoken sounds like ANTIBACT; AERIAL loses its first letter to give ERIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Antibacterial describes a type of household cleaner or spray that kills germs.

clue.text: Making slight tweaks initially in medication, adding grams

indicators.note: the first letter of tweaks goes within the medication

parts.note: insulin is a medication for diabetes

indicators.note: initially means the first letter

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grams

explanation.surface: Adjusting a dose of medicine by adding a few grams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making slight' is the definition: to slight someone is to insult them.
explanation.definitionFit: To slight someone is to snub or offend them, so making a slight is being offensive.

clue.text: Club closed during utter shambles

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so these go inside

parts.note: to air an opinion is to utter it
a bat is a club
a door pushed to is closed

explanation.surface: A nightclub shuts in the middle of a complete mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shambles' is an old word for a slaughterhouse, not a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: A shambles was originally a meat market and then a slaughterhouse, which an abattoir is.

clue.text: Colt's head sports scar, bone repeatedly bashed climbing these?

indicators.note: something bashed is knocked out of shape, so the letters are reshaped
a head is at the top, so the first letter

parts.note: repeatedly says the word bone comes again, a second copy
bone taken as written

explanation.surface: A young horse, scarred and with a bashed bone, has a nasty fall while climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: C, the head of 'Colt's', joins SCAR plus BONE twice, and 'bashed' rearranges the lot. The Brecon Beacons are a mountain range in south Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brecon Beacons are Welsh mountains popular with hill walkers, so climbing them is a natural pastime.

clue.text: Buddy on drums supporting band on street flier? Not so

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath

parts.note: O looks like a ring or band
Buddy Rich was a jazz drummer

explanation.surface: A friend drumming in a street band gets airborne, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: Buddy Rich was an American big-band drummer. 'flier? Not so' points to a bird that cannot fly.
explanation.definitionFit: The ostrich is a flightless bird, so it is a bird that is not a flier.

clue.text: Scandinavian regrets twisting lower half — reason for injury?

parts.note: Ove is a Scandinavian man's name

indicators.note: the lower half of a down word is its last two letters, and these swap places

parts.note: rues means regrets

explanation.surface: A Norseman regrets twisting his lower body, the cause of injury.
explanation.definitionFit: Overuse, as in repetitive strain, is a common cause of sports injuries.

clue.text: Wet resident of lake changing name to Jack

indicators.note: one letter changes for another, the name's letter becoming Jack's

parts.note: Nessie is the monster said to live in Loch Ness
J is the abbreviation for jack in cards

explanation.surface: Something damp lives in a lake and swaps its name for Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wet' means feeble; a jessie is British slang for a weak or soppy man.
explanation.definitionFit: A jessie is British slang for a feeble, unmanly person, which is what wet means as a noun.

clue.text: Children outside swinging, so thrilled?

indicators.note: the children are placed around the other piece

parts.note: tots are small children
swinging both ways is slang for bisexual, BI

explanation.surface: Kids playing outside on swings are delighted.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition completes a phrase: 'thrilled to bits' means delighted.
explanation.definitionFit: In the idiom 'thrilled to bits', the answer is what follows the adjective, so it stands for being so pleased.

clue.text: Be thankful for B minus

parts.note: minus means less

explanation.surface: Be grateful for a B-minus grade.
explanation.definitionFit: To bless something is to give thanks for it, as in counting your blessings.

clue.text: Adult runner crossing over to get shade

indicators.note: the two pieces cross over, swapping places from the order Blue Nile

parts.note: a river runs, and the Nile is one
blue means adult in the sense of risqué, as in a blue film

explanation.surface: A grown-up runner crosses a line to win a coloured prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adult runner' reads as the Blue Nile, the river; the pieces swap over to give the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Nile blue is a pale greenish-blue colour, so it is a particular shade.

clue.text: Purchase confused Chas leaving Amazon here

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled into a new order
leaving signals the named letters depart from the pool

explanation.surface: A muddled shopper called Chas abandons an Amazon order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amazon' looks like the online retailer; it is the river. Remove CHAS from PURCHASE and rearrange PURE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amazon river rises in the Andes of this South American country, so it is found there.

clue.text: Crack even parts to founder Titanic?

indicators.note: the even-numbered letters, second, fourth and sixth, of founder

parts.note: the Titanic was an ocean liner, an example

explanation.surface: A wisecrack about a ship that sank on its maiden voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'founder' looks like the sinking of the Titanic; it is just the word whose even letters O, N, E are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack is a quip, and a one-liner is a short joke delivered in a single sentence.

clue.text: Vegan produce Navy rejected, standing by its nautical practice

indicators.note: the navy is thrown out, so its letters are removed

parts.note: Quorn is a brand of meat-free food
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: The navy turns down vegetarian food served beside its usual ship's routine.
explanation.walkthrough: Quorn is a meat-substitute brand made from mycoprotein; 'standing by' is a link, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Quoits, throwing rope rings at a peg, was a traditional game played on board ship, hence deck quoits.

clue.text: Back-to-back games keeping mum at house busy then

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside

parts.note: RU is rugby union, games, followed by the same letters turned back
mum, as in keep mum, is silence, SH

explanation.surface: Consecutive matches keep a mother at home, a busy time.
explanation.walkthrough: RU, rugby union, followed by RU reversed puts the two back to back.
explanation.definitionFit: The rush hour is the time when traffic and commuters are at their peak, so roads are busy.

clue.text: Fit core of athletes leading around three miles once

indicators.note: the core goes in front of the fit
the core of a word is its centre, the middle two letters here

parts.note: an ague is a fit of shivering fever

explanation.surface: A fit athlete leads round a three-mile course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' looks like describing the athletes; it is the fever.
explanation.definitionFit: A league was an old measure of distance, roughly three miles.
